Subject: Credit offset framework and pricing ladder — mechanics and examples

Hi Samantha / Helix procurement team,

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, I wanted to put a short note on the proposed mechanics for handling variances against committed usage and outline how credits, roll-forwards, and the pricing ladder would operate in practice. This is focused on Hosted API (per-token) usage and the committed tiers we sketched.

High level proposal (summary):
- Quarterly measurement windows with a 30-day administrative period to issue credits for underutilization.
- Annual final true-up that reconciles quarterly credits against annual committed dollars; if Helix still falls short on aggregate annual usage, Redwood issues a make-good credit (non-cash) or applies a one-time invoice credit, per the table below.
- Credits can be rolled forward up to 25% of the next quarter's committed tokens cap; credits expire after 12 months if not consumed.
- No cash refunds; credits apply only to Hosted API per-token invoices or Marketplace fees.

Questions we need from you to finalize:
1) Would Procurement accept credits (non-refundable) that can be applied to future Hosted API invoices?
2) Any internal constraints on credits rolling across fiscal years?
3) Is a quarterly invoice cadence (net 30) compatible with your AR process?

Attached: Helix_Commit_Summary_Q1Q2.xlsx (your committed bands + our usage projection), and a draft credit ladder (redwood_proposed_credit_table.pdf). The ladder maps committed tier -> per-token discount -> excess-tier surcharge.

I propose a short call with legal/procurement to lock wording for the SOW clause that covers: measurement window, credit issuance timing, rollforward cap, and final annual true-up mechanics. Would Thu 10/12 11:00am PT work?

Thanks — I want to keep the mechanics simple so your finance team can model the cashflow impact.

Best,

Raf / Marissa — quick internal note with recommended approach to present to Helix: 

Proposed mechanics (concise):
- Measurement: Quarter-level usage measurement (calendar quarter). Total tokens billed vs committed tokens for that quarter.
- Credit issuance: If billed tokens < committed tokens, Redwood issues a credit equal to the token shortfall multiplied by the committed-tier effective per-token rate. Credits issued within 30 days after quarter close.
- Annual true-up: At year-end, if aggregate billed tokens < aggregate committed tokens, Redwood issues a make-good credit per the ladder. Credits are non-refundable, apply to future Hosted API charges.
- Rollforward: Credits may roll forward but capped at 25% of the following quarter's committed tokens to avoid large multi-quarter deferrals. Unused credits beyond cap expire after 12 months.
- Mid-quarter changes: Treat reductions as effective the next quarter unless both parties sign an amendment. This avoids constant churn.

Examples to include in the Helix packet: 
- Example A: Q1 commit 1B tokens, actual 800M -> credit = 200M * committed-rate -> applied to Q2 invoices until consumed up to 25% cap.
- Example B: Annual: 4B committed vs 3.4B consumed across quarters -> make-good credit applied during Q1 of the following year per ladder.

Operational asks for Helix:
1) Can Procurement confirm quarterly invoice cadence (net 30)?
2) Will Finance accept non-cash credits vs a cash refund? We recommend non-cash credits to keep invoicing flow simple.
3) Legal will want SOW language; propose Redwood drafts sample clause for review.

I attached a tighter credit table showing hypothetical dollar impacts for each band (sending to Raf to include with Helix packet). Keep messaging straightforward: credits protect both parties and simplify accounting vs manual refunds.

—Vanessa Ortiz

Hi Sam / Alex / procurement —

Thanks for the quick review and the questions. Below are our answers and the consolidated proposal. I also adjusted the DocuSign template to include the SOW clause language Alex might need (link below).

Direct answers:
- Mid-quarter reductions: We treat the originally committed quarter as fixed unless both parties sign an amendment. Any committed-tier change takes effect the next quarter. This keeps the measurement windows clean for billing and audit.
- Expiry vs rollforward: Credits issued are valid for 12 months from issue date. Rollforward cap is 25% of the next quarter's committed tokens; any amount beyond the cap expires and is not convertible to cash.
- Accounting ledger: Redwood will provide a credits ledger (CSV) that maps each issued credit to the invoice(s) it was applied to, including invoice numbers and dates. That ledger will be produced within 30 days of credit issuance.

Consolidated mechanics (what we will put in SOW):
1) Quarterly measurement, 30-day credit issuance window.
2) Credits are non-cash, apply to future Hosted API invoices, expire after 12 months.
3) Rollforward cap = 25% of following quarter committed tokens; unused beyond cap expire.
4) Annual final true-up to compute any additional make-good credits; applied in Q1 of the subsequent year.
5) Mid-quarter changes require mutual written amendment to take effect mid-window.

Next steps:
- Alex: I attached a short SOW clause draft and the DocuSign link for your internal review: https://www.docusign.com/helixtemplate/rl-99812
- Sam / Procurement: confirm whether 10:00am PT Thu 10/12 works; if so, I’ll send a calendar invite and a 1-page summary for your CFO.

Best,
Rafael
